statement: How each REPDF class changes the bytes (all 1,000 files vs their originals): C1 overwrites 11-12 of the first 12 bytes; C2 removes 2.4-39 KB (the classic xref); C3 removes 23-215 bytes; C4 removes 45-128 bytes around the page tree; C5 removes exactly 8 bytes (an object header); C10 keeps exactly 70% of bytes.
result: Per class x creation method (min/median/max in summary.json). C1: 12-byte span, 11-12 differing bytes. C5: size delta -8 in all 100 files. C10: kept fraction 0.7 in all 100 files. C2 saveas -21294..-39094 bytes, print -2452..-3972. C3 saveas -210..-215, print -23..-24. C4 -45..-128.

statement: REPDF's C9 files are not single-byte corruptions: each of the 100 C9 files differs from its original in 12-30 bytes spread across 11-28 distinct stream bodies (size unchanged), contradicting the paper's 'modifying a random byte' (CLM-0026).
result: C9/saveas diff_bytes 13/21/29, streams_hit 11/17/28; C9/print diff_bytes 12/22.5/30, streams_hit 12/18/26 (min/median/max). Replacement bytes are varied (top replacement byte covers <=4% of changes).

statement: REPDF's C7 and C8 do not delete font data: they overwrite it in place with ASCII spaces (0x20), keeping the file size, so every xref offset stays valid. 100% of changed bytes are 0x20 in all 200 C7/C8 files.
result: C7 saveas/print and C8 saveas/print: size_delta 0 in all files; top replacement byte 0x20 with share 1.0 in every file; changed bytes 165 KB-2.9 MB per file; C7 touches 11-22 streams, C8 19-44 (adds ToUnicode).

statement: Header loss alone (REPDF C1) makes the default Ghostscript 10.02.1 CLI fail on 100/100 files (the input is sniffed as PostScript); forcing the PDF interpreter recovers all 100, but adding xref loss (C1+C2 compound) makes forced Ghostscript fail on 100/100 while still exiting 0, matching the source rule that pdfi repair needs a '%PDF' somewhere in the file (CLM-0540). MuPDF recovers 100/100 in every variant; pdftotext 94/100 for header-damaged variants.

inputs.note: REPDF dataset (SRC-0002), git commit e547d4d1b77ead7e8cccce8b02878a6d33aa427a; 100 documents x {original, _header (C1), _xref (C2), compound C2-with-C1-header built in a temp dir}

result: Recovered (extracted non-whitespace text >= 0.95 of the same tool's text from the original), out of 100 per variant. original: mutool 100, gs 100, gs forced 100, pdftotext 100 (qpdf exit 0 for all). C1: mutool 100, gs 0 (all nonzero exit, input treated as PostScript), gs forced 100, pdftotext 94 (6 Print-to-PDF files keep 79-90% of the text; in the one file inspected, pdftotext reported an xref reconstruction and a missing font resource), qpdf exit 3 (warnings) for all. C2: all four 100. C1+C2: mutool 100, gs 0, gs forced 0 with exit code 0 ('Catalog dictionary not located in file'), pdftotext 94, qpdf exit 3 for all. No file in C1 or C1+C2 contains '%PDF' anywhere.
